It's surprisingly simple and legal, you order some pods (make sure they're papaver somniferum) from an online florist. Be careful with the dosage as the potency can vary, 1-3 medium (size of a walnut) pods is the amount recommended for someone starting. Also check out the 'recipes' on erowid, they're extremely helpful.

In addition to what OP said, you can buy unwashed poppy seeds online and use them the same way.

Google Papaver Somniferum and take note of the leaves near the base of the plant and how the crowns on the pods themselves look. Then go for a walk around a neighborhood that has NOT been built in the last 10 years and you are sure to find a shit ton of pods!

If being a garden ninja is not your game then go canvess grocery stores looking in their bulk section for poppy seeds. If they are black/blue/grey and have a tiny bit of straw (dried plant matter) in them you are good to go! Wash those seeds in a two litre pop bottle and drink the nasty brew. Prepare to feel amazing!

It is traditionally called "Poppy Seed Tea", "Poppy Pod Tea" or "Doda". What you end up drinking is the real deal....opium! Of course if you want to argue semantics it is not TRUE opium since you couldn't just smoke it but the alkaloids are pretty much the exact same. Morphine and codeine are all part of the opium poppy and will be all present when you eat/drink something like this! There are like 12+ alkaloids present in the opium poppy that act as agonists/antagonists as well. They use the same liver enzymes to break down as morphine does so oral opium will last a fucking long time. Like 24+ hours long since the liver is busy processing a shit ton of other alkaloids alongside morphine.

Good ol Opium tea! My absolute favorite drug of all time! So easy to get, so fucking cheap (free in the growing season!) and it keeps you high for 24 hours! Is there really a better drug out there? I mean sure.....you don't get the rushing euphoria like doing a shot of heroin but my gaawd! I would much rather be on a soft pillow for 24+hours than on the worlds most amazing feather bed for only a couple of hours.

[ACOK] Who is your favorite faction to start out with?

Sorry tried answering yesterday, but the because of the server crash it didn't go through.

It depends what you mean with by "start out with". If by joining a faction as a vassal I'd have to say the Targaryen faction, or the Iron Islands are the most fun to play.

However if you mean troop composition then I'd say I'd begin with a army consisting solely of Reach levies. At first this might sound strange , but I've found and army consisting of solely Reach soilders to be highly effective early to mid game.

Reach glaivemen are highly effective dealing with the wildling horsemen which makes hunting parties of wildlings in the north highly effective early on destroying larger parties with minimal casualties even with full damage on your soilders. Because of this constant conflict with minimal casualties you can pretty quickly get an army of knights and elite glaivemen.

Generally I let the wildling horsemen spear themselves of the glaivemen, and swing my knights around the side, and decimate their footmen. Because of this 50 reach soldiers can defeat an equal number of wildlings with zero losses most of the time. The profits you make from such can easily buy your first few enterprises.

Once you've secured your position I'd probably go with a mixed composition of reach knights, ironborn retainers, and bowmen (I generally go with bowmen from the vale).

I hope somebody finds this useful. If you've read my long boring rant thus far thanks

If you want the strongest units in each class this is a good starting position. Especially if you are not a monarch. When you become a monarch the player faction long bowmen are the strongest in the game. Followed closely by the valemen.

Elite iron born retainers are terrifying. Their lack of shields is a big drawback though. I use them until I get a fair amount of money then I conisitantly buy unsullied and use them as my sole infantry. Unsullied are pricey though and I'm approaching day 900.

How you generally start off your first kingdom? Before 2.0 what I did was beat the wights easily, get the fire pots, and absolutely annihilate the first city I take with said fire pots. Now though fighting the wights is insane. I'm making over 10k a week in profits, but even a massive fully trained army can't seem to beat the wights now

I raise an army of the troops you first mentioned first. Then I take a Dragonstone castle while they are spread thin fighting everyone. Dragonstone is by far the weakest faction on that side of the sea. Where you go from there is whatever you want. I make a few of the knight companions that I got with the money I won from tournaments vassals and have them follow me around. I now make around 20-30k a week. It varies wildly between that.

I just hate getting a massive enough army to take a castle because it seems like you spend more time moving from town to town to find food than you actually spend fighting. I prefer a decent sized extremely elite and mobile army while my vassals act as the wall fodder. That's why I like using the fire pots to start out my empire.

So how do you keep your army supplies? It seems like in my game nobody ever has enough food for sale. Or how do you beat the wights?

If you are at war and winning battles you wont need food. Morale will go down but will be instantly replenished by a victory. Also if you have time you can Only bring in your archers and clear the walls. After your archers run out of arrows just retreat and you'll still gain morale as long as you killed more than they did. You can repeat this until their defense has dwindled. If you don't have a good engineer that could take some time as you'll be building ladders repeatedly.

I started learning piano back from Alfred basic piano library (currently end of level 2). Most songs kinda of sucks and feel very childish. So do you know any easy to learn songs that just sound great?
Do you guys know any easy to learn piano songs?

Yes. These are "easy" classical pieces, and might be a little challenging (but that's good for you) and they are infinitely better than the pieces in those books.

In order of least to most difficult: (Note: Pdf files; all from imslp.org)

Bach Prelude in C from The Well-Tempered Clavier

2 Minuets by Petzold

Chopin Prelude No. 4 in E minor

Bach Invention No. 1 in C

Brahms waltzes (The easiest are No. 9 in D minor, No. 2 in G-sharp minor, and No. 15 in A-flat major, in that order. The rest of them are more difficult.)

Beethoven Moonlight Sonata, 1st Movement

Haydn Keyboard Sonata in F major, Hob.XVI:23 (Larghetto only; starts on page 8)

Chopin Nocturne in E-flat, Op.9 No. 2

Liszt Consolations No. 1 and No. 3

Beethoven Piano Sonata No.20, Op.49 No.2 in G

Beethoven Piano Sonata No.20, Op.49 No.1 in G Minor

Also look up the sonatas of Domenico Scarlatti on Youtube and find the ones you like on imslp.org. There are a LOT of them, ranging from very easy to very difficult.

If you have a midi or usb-capable keyboard, Synthesia is excellent. You -can- use it in conjunction with reading music, but the default system it uses is more intuitive than the standard lattice orientation. You would be limiting yourself by not practicing from sheets, but if you're all right with that, you can make rapid progress this way. It's basically DDR/Guitar Hero for piano, and actually teaches you how to play real songs. As for which songs to play-- I'd recommend checking youtube for some Synthesia videos of songs you like by searching for the artist/title + easy synthesia tutorial. It makes such a difference having horizontally-oriented music for a horizontally-oriented instrument. You CAN use synthesia without a midi-usb capable keyboard, but you wouldn't get the same fast progress out of it. Take a look!
